themes_detail.label: Tree Crisis in Park Slope
themes_detail.summary: Dead and dying trees spiked to 10 complaints this week versus a baseline of 1.4 per week—a 627% increase (z-score: 10.06)—signaling a potential disease outbreak, storm damage, or neglect crisis affecting the neighborhood's canopy this week.
evidence: 10 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (627% spike)
Z-score of 10.06 indicates extremely rare statistical anomaly
Community Board has repeatedly requested park reconstruction/upgrades, suggesting existing maintenance issues
343 total damaged tree complaints over 90 days indicates ongoing baseline problem
reporting_angles: What triggered the sudden spike—disease, pest infestation, recent weather event, or deferred maintenance?
Interview Parks Department on tree health assessment and removal/replanting timeline
Investigate whether this correlates with Prospect Park or neighborhood-specific tree canopy loss

themes_detail.label: Street Deterioration Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints jumped to 30 this past week versus a 5.6 weekly baseline—a 433% spike (z-score: 7.27)—suggesting rapid street surface degradation or pothole formation across Park Slope this past week.
evidence: 30 curb condition complaints last week vs. 5.6 weekly average (433% increase)
Z-score of 7.27 indicates statistically extreme outlier
Street Condition remains top-tier complaint category overall (604 complaints in 90 days)
Snow/Ice complaints (549 total) suggest winter damage may be accelerating curb deterioration
reporting_angles: Are winter conditions exposing pre-existing infrastructure failure, or is this new damage?
Compare 311 complaints to DOT repair timelines and street resurfacing schedules in the district
Visual documentation of affected blocks and resident safety impact

themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining/Vendor Chaos
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints surged to 7 this past 2 weeks versus 0.8 weekly baseline (833% increase), while vendor enforcement issues hit 4 complaints this week versus 0.5 average (700% spike)—signaling enforcement gaps or quality-of-life conflicts around informal street commerce over the past 2 weeks.
evidence: 7 outdoor dining complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly average (833% spike, z-score: 4.81)
4 vendor enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (700% increase, z-score: 4.95)
Two separate complaint categories spiking in parallel suggests systemic enforcement or compliance issue
Active ULURP and rezoning applications (46 Nelson Street, GSD Waterfront) may indicate changing commercial landscape
reporting_angles: Are new or expanded outdoor dining setups violating sidewalk/fire codes or creating noise/sanitation issues?
Interview affected residents and business owners about specific vendor or restaurant complaints
Investigate whether Parks Dept and DSNY enforcement staffing is adequate for this emerging activity

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Disruption
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints jumped to 3 this past week versus 0.4 weekly baseline (700% increase, z-score: 5.42), signaling an emerging quality-of-life issue in Prospect Park or neighborhood green spaces this week.
evidence: 3 park noise complaints last week vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 5.42)
Community Board has requested enhanced park safety through security staff—suggests existing concerns
Outdoor dining spike (same timeframe) may indicate increased foot traffic and social activity in parks
Residential and general noise complaints remain elevated overall (589 and 560 complaints in 90 days)
reporting_angles: What specific activities or hours are generating noise complaints—music, events, social gatherings?
Interview Parks enforcement on weekend/evening patrol capacity in Prospect Park
Are there unauthorized or inadequately permitted events happening in park spaces?

themes_detail.label: Unsanitary Conditions Rising
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary condition complaints hit 29 complaints 3 weeks ago versus a 12.2 weekly baseline (137% increase, z-score: 5.18), indicating a potential garbage collection, rodent, or street cleanliness crisis that may still be unresolved.
evidence: 29 unsanitary condition complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 12.2 weekly average (137% spike, z-score: 5.18)
Dirty Condition complaints remain significant (315 total over 90 days)
Water System complaints (353 total) may indicate sewage or drainage issues contributing to sanitation problems
Community Board requests for homeless services suggest encampment-related sanitation stress
reporting_angles: Has DSNY collection frequency or staffing changed, or are there specific sanitation hotspots?
Are homeless encampments or informal settlements creating concentrated unsanitary conditions?
Investigate whether this spike has subsided or persists into current week
